title: For Leaders, the Opposite of Belief Is Never Disbelief
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This post claims that leaders live in a state of commitment: when they lose confidence in a belief, they do not drift into doubt but immediately adopt a new belief. Commitment to a firm point of view, the author argues, is what separates leaders from others and is a precondition for strategy, vision, confidence and execution plans. That commitment comes from the importance of commitment itself rather than from experience or aptitude. He ties this to the popular maxim of strong opinions held weakly, while observing that in practice leaders are heavy on opinion and light on adjustment. The piece is a character sketch of the leader as someone who is always in.
points: When a leader gives up a cherished belief, the replacement is a new belief, not uncertainty.
A committed point of view is a prerequisite for creating strategy, articulating vision and projecting confidence.
The author says commitment arises from the importance of commitment itself, not from experience, aptitude or character.
Leaders land hard on a belief but do not stay longer than they should, echoing the maxim of strong opinions held weakly.
quotes: They simply give up on a cherished belief and replace it with a new and refurbished way of thinking. They commit to the new belief. Leaders, above all, understand that the opposite of belief is not disbelief; it is belief in something else.

True leaders live in a state of commitment to ideas, people, and assumptions. Whenever they have doubts or lose confidence in something, they immediately look for an alternative. They don’t wallow in self-doubt or uncertainty. Because they have a bias for action, they can’t exist without a commitment to a point of view.

Commitment to a set of beliefs and a firm point of view is largely what separates leaders from those who don’t have such a commitment. It is nearly impossible to create strategy, articulate vision, project confidence, and design a plan for execution without a strong commitment to a view.

Leaders attach themselves to people, ideas, and beliefs they can be committed to. In essence, they are on a continual search for belief. When they land, they land hard, with both feet making an imprint.
Perhaps that is why the expression “Strong opinions held weakly” is so popular with leaders across the globe. Of course, in reality, the recipe is heavy on opinion and light on adjustment.
